translations.title: Liftoff
translations.story: A C countdown from 1972. Make it run on a Dartmouth terminal from 1964.
translations.task: Write the same countdown in BASIC with a FOR loop and STEP.
hints: C's for (i = 10; i >= 1; i--) is FOR I = 10 TO 1 STEP -1 in BASIC.
The loop body ends with NEXT I.
Don't forget END.

translations.title: Squares Table
translations.story: A FORTRAN table of squares, punched on cards in 1957. Type it in BASIC.
translations.task: Print the same table: each number from 1 to 5 and its square, two numbers per line.
translations.source:
DO 10 I = 1, 5
      J = I * I
      WRITE (6,20) I, J
   10 CONTINUE
   20 FORMAT (1X, I3, I5)
      STOP
      END
hints: The DO loop becomes FOR I = 1 TO 5 … NEXT I.
PRINT I, I * I prints both numbers on one line.
The spacing doesn't have to match exactly.

translations.title: Sum to Twenty
translations.story: On the KIM-1, this took a loop and the carry flag. In BASIC it's much shorter.
translations.task: The 6502 program adds 20 + 19 + … + 1 and stores the result at $0301. Do the same in BASIC with a loop, and PRINT the result.
translations.source:
LDA #0
        LDX #20
LOOP:   STX $30
        CLC
        ADC $30
        DEX
        BNE LOOP
        STA $0301
        BRK

requirements.message: Add up with a FOR loop, not with a formula.

hints: A is the running sum: LET S = 0.
X counts down from 20, but you can count up: FOR I = 1 TO 20.
LET S = S + I inside the loop, PRINT S after it.

translations.title: Euclid
translations.story: Euclid's algorithm for the greatest common divisor is 2,300 years old. Here it is in C; Dartmouth BASIC has no % operator.
translations.task: Write Euclid's algorithm in BASIC for 1071 and 462 and print GCD = 21. Use INT to get the remainder: R = A - INT(A / B) * B.

requirements.message: Loop with IF … THEN and GOTO.

hints: BASIC has no while: test IF B = 0 THEN jump to the PRINT.
LET R = A - INT(A / B) * B is the remainder.
Then A = B, B = R, and GOTO back to the test.

translations.title: Average from Cards
translations.story: The FORTRAN version keeps its numbers in a DATA statement. BASIC has READ and DATA for that.
translations.task: Read the same six numbers with READ and DATA, and print their sum and their whole-number average on two lines.
translations.source:
DIMENSION K(6)
      DATA K / 12, 17, 9, 21, 15, 16 /
      ISUM = 0
      DO 10 I = 1, 6
      ISUM = ISUM + K(I)
   10 CONTINUE
      IAVG = ISUM / 6
      WRITE (6,20) ISUM
      WRITE (6,20) IAVG
   20 FORMAT (1X, I5)
      STOP
      END

requirements.message: Put the numbers in a DATA line.

hints: DATA 12, 17, 9, 21, 15, 16 holds the numbers.
In a FOR loop: READ X and add it to S.
PRINT S and PRINT S / 6 after the loop.

translations.title: Celsius Table
translations.story: A BASIC temperature table. On the IBM 704 it needs a DO loop and a FORMAT.
translations.task: Print the same table with a DO loop: Celsius 0, 10 … 40 and Fahrenheit (C * 9 / 5 + 32), two whole numbers per line.
translations.source:
10 FOR C = 0 TO 40 STEP 10
20 PRINT C, C * 9 / 5 + 32
30 NEXT C
40 END
hints: DO 10 IC = 0, 40, 10 counts in steps of 10. Names starting with I to N are whole numbers.
Compute the Fahrenheit value into another integer variable.
WRITE (6,20) with 20 FORMAT (1X, I4, I5).

translations.title: Factorials
translations.story: C would use recursion. FORTRAN IV can't call itself, so it multiplies in a loop.
translations.task: Print n and n! for n = 1 to 7, two numbers per line, with a DO loop.
hints: Keep the running product in an integer variable: NF = 1.
Each round: NF = NF * N, then WRITE.
FORMAT (1X, I2, I6) is wide enough for 5040.

translations.title: Multiply by Adding
translations.story: The 6502 has no multiply instruction, so this program adds 13 eleven times. The IBM 704 could multiply, but let's copy the idea.
translations.task: Compute 13 × 11 the same way, by adding 13 eleven times in a DO loop, and print the result.
translations.source:
LDA #0
        LDX #11
LOOP:   CLC
        ADC #13
        DEX
        BNE LOOP
        STA $0301
        BRK
hints: Start with K = 0.
DO 10 I = 1, 11 with K = K + 13 inside.
WRITE K after the loop.

translations.title: Biggest of Three
translations.story: BASIC jumps around with IF … THEN line numbers. FORTRAN IV's logical IF can do a whole statement.
translations.task: Find the biggest of 17, 42 and 23 with logical IFs and print MAX = 42.
translations.source:
10 LET A = 17
20 LET B = 42
30 LET C = 23
40 LET M = A
50 IF B <= M THEN 70
60 LET M = B
70 IF C <= M THEN 90
80 LET M = C
90 PRINT "MAX = "; M
100 END

requirements.message: Compare with a logical IF and .GT.

hints: Whole numbers need names starting with I to N, like IA, IB, IC and M.
IF (IB .GT. M) M = IB
10 FORMAT (' MAX =', I4)

translations.title: Hypotenuse
translations.story: A C function returns the long side of a right triangle. FORTRAN can do it in one line with a statement function.
translations.task: Write a statement function for the hypotenuse and print it for 3, 4 and for 5, 12 with two decimals.

requirements.message: Define a statement function, like H(A, B) = …

hints: The statement function comes first: H(A, B) = SQRT(A * A + B * B)
Call it like a function: X = H(3.0, 4.0)
F6.2 prints two decimals.

translations.title: Gauss
translations.story: Little Gauss supposedly added 1 to 100 in his head. Here's the BASIC way; now the C way.
translations.task: Add up 1 to 100 with a for loop and print 5050.
translations.source:
10 LET S = 0
20 FOR I = 1 TO 100
30 LET S = S + I
40 NEXT I
50 PRINT S
60 END
hints: int i, s = 0;
printf("%d\n", s);

translations.title: The Three-Way IF
translations.story: FORTRAN's IF jumps to one of three labels: negative, zero or positive. C needs if and else if.
translations.task: Put the same numbers in an int array and print NEGATIVE, ZERO or POSITIVE for each, with if / else if / else.
translations.source:
DIMENSION K(3)
      DATA K / -3, 0, 7 /
      DO 40 I = 1, 3
      IF (K(I)) 10, 20, 30
   10 WRITE (6,51)
      GO TO 40
   20 WRITE (6,52)
      GO TO 40
   30 WRITE (6,53)
   40 CONTINUE
   51 FORMAT (' NEGATIVE')
   52 FORMAT (' ZERO')
   53 FORMAT (' POSITIVE')
      STOP
      END
hints: int k[3] = {-3, 0, 7}; FORTRAN counts from 1, C from 0.
Loop with for (i = 0; i < 3; i++).
if (k[i] < 0) … else if (k[i] == 0) … else …

translations.title: GOSUB to Function
translations.story: BASIC subroutines share all variables and are called with GOSUB. C has real functions with parameters.
translations.task: Write void stars(int n) and use it to print the same three rows.
translations.source:
10 LET N = 3
20 GOSUB 100
30 LET N = 5
40 GOSUB 100
50 LET N = 7
60 GOSUB 100
70 STOP
100 FOR I = 1 TO N
110 PRINT "*";
120 NEXT I
130 PRINT
140 RETURN
150 END
hints: Instead of LET N = 3 and GOSUB 100, call stars(3).
Inside: a for loop with putchar('*'), then a newline.

translations.title: Count the Bits
translations.story: The 6502 shifts the byte right and counts the carries. C's >> and & do the same.
translations.task: Count the 1 bits of 177 the same way (shift right, look at the lowest bit) and print 4.
translations.source:
LDA #177
        LDX #0
        LDY #8
LOOP:   LSR A
        BCC SKIP
        INX
SKIP:   DEY
        BNE LOOP
        STX $0301
        BRK

requirements.message: Look at the lowest bit with & 1.

hints: LSR A is n >>= 1, and the bit that falls out is n & 1.
Count it when it's 1, eight times.

translations.title: Newton's Square Root
translations.story: Isaac Newton's method, as the IBM 704 ran it in 1957. C's double has even more digits.
translations.task: Run the same 5 steps for the square root of 2 in C and print the step number and the value with 8 decimals.
translations.source:
A = 2.0
      X = 1.0
      DO 10 I = 1, 5
      X = (X + A / X) / 2.0
      WRITE (6,20) I, X
   10 CONTINUE
   20 FORMAT (1X, I2, F12.8)
      STOP
      END
hints: double a = 2.0, x = 1.0;
x = (x + a / x) / 2.0; inside the loop.
printf("%d %.8f\n", i, x);
translations.sourceNote: The FORTRAN REAL keeps only about 7 digits, so its last digits are a little off. Your C program uses double, with about 16 digits: it prints the exact values.

translations.title: Eight Stars
translations.story: On the KIM-1 there is no PRINT: each character goes to the teletype with JSR OUTCH.
translations.task: Print the same eight stars with a loop. End with BRK.
translations.source:
10 FOR I = 1 TO 8
20 PRINT "*";
30 NEXT I
40 END
hints: LDX #8 counts the stars, LDA #'* is the character.
LOOP: JSR OUTCH, DEX, BNE LOOP.
Then BRK.

translations.title: Digits Down
translations.story: putchar('0' + i) turns a number into a digit. On the 6502 that's ADC #'0.
translations.task: Print 9876543210 like the C program does. End with BRK.

requirements.message: Turn the number into a digit with ADC #'0.

hints: Count down in X from 9.
Each round: TXA, CLC, ADC #'0, JSR OUTCH.
DEX, BPL LOOP keeps going down to 0.

translations.title: Sum to Ten
translations.story: The FORTRAN program prints the sum. On the 6502, leave it in memory instead.
translations.task: Add up 1 to 10 like the FORTRAN program, but store the result at $0300. End with BRK.
translations.source:
ISUM = 0
      DO 10 I = 1, 10
      ISUM = ISUM + I
   10 CONTINUE
      WRITE (6,20) ISUM
   20 FORMAT (1X, I4)
      STOP
      END
hints: A holds the sum, X counts down from 10.
Loop: STX $30, CLC, ADC $30, DEX, BNE LOOP.
STA $0300, BRK.

translations.title: The Biggest Number
translations.story: BASIC READs its numbers from DATA. On the 6502, the five numbers are already in memory at $0300–$0304.
translations.task: Find the biggest of the five bytes at $0300–$0304, like the BASIC program does, and store it at $0310. End with BRK.
translations.source:
10 READ M
20 FOR I = 2 TO 5
30 READ X
40 IF X <= M THEN 60
50 LET M = X
60 NEXT I
70 PRINT M
80 DATA 3, 9, 4, 12, 7
90 END
hints: Start with LDA $0300 (like READ M) and LDX #1.
CMP $0300,X sets the carry when A is bigger or equal: BCS SKIP.
Otherwise LDA $0300,X. Then INX, CPX #5, BNE LOOP, STA $0310.

translations.title: Times Ten with Shifts
translations.story: A clever C trick: x * 10 is x * 8 + x * 2, and both are just shifts. The 6502 has ASL for that.
translations.task: The number at $0300 is 0 to 25. Store it times ten at $0301, with ASL and ADC, no loop of additions. End with BRK.
hints: ASL A doubles A. Save x * 2 in $30.
Two more ASLs make x * 8.
CLC, ADC $30 adds x * 2: that's x * 10.

translations.title: Times Seven
translations.story: A Dartmouth BASIC loop from 1964. In Turbo Pascal it's a for loop.
translations.task: Print the same five multiples of 7, one per line, with a for loop.
translations.source:
10 FOR I = 1 TO 5
20 PRINT I * 7
30 NEXT I
40 END
hints: FOR I = 1 TO 5 becomes for i := 1 to 5 do.
PRINT becomes writeln, and NEXT I disappears.

translations.title: FizzBuzz
translations.story: The classic programming test, in C. Pascal has no % and no &&: it uses mod and and.
translations.task: Print the same 15 lines in Pascal with a for loop and if … else if.
translations.expectedOutput:
1
2
Fizz
4
Buzz
Fizz
7
8
Fizz
Buzz
11
Fizz
13
14
FizzBuzz
hints: i % 3 == 0 is i mod 3 = 0 in Pascal.
No ; before else!
translations.sourceOutput:
1
2
Fizz
4
Buzz
Fizz
7
8
Fizz
Buzz
11
Fizz
13
14
FizzBuzz

translations.title: Average from DATA
translations.story: FORTRAN keeps its numbers in a DATA statement. Pascal can do the same with a typed array constant.
translations.task: Put the same six numbers in a typed constant array[1..6] of integer, then print their sum and their whole-number average (with div), like the FORTRAN program.
translations.source:
DIMENSION K(6)
      DATA K / 12, 17, 9, 21, 15, 16 /
      ISUM = 0
      DO 10 I = 1, 6
      ISUM = ISUM + K(I)
   10 CONTINUE
      WRITE (6,20) ISUM
      WRITE (6,20) ISUM / 6
   20 FORMAT (1X, I5)
      STOP
      END

requirements.message: Use div for the whole-number average.

hints: const k: array[1..6] of integer = (12, 17, 9, 21, 15, 16);
FORTRAN's integer division is div in Pascal.

translations.title: Count the Bits
translations.story: The 6502 shifts the byte right and counts the carries. Pascal can do it with mod 2 and div 2.
translations.task: Count the 1 bits of 177 the same way, with a while loop (n mod 2 is the bit that falls out, n div 2 shifts right), and print 4.
translations.source:
LDA #177
        LDX #0
        LDY #8
LOOP:   LSR A
        BCC SKIP
        INX
SKIP:   DEY
        BNE LOOP
        STX $0301
        BRK

requirements.message: Look at the lowest bit with mod 2.

hints: LSR is n := n div 2, and the carry is n mod 2.
Count while n > 0.

translations.title: Structs to Records
translations.story: C's struct and Pascal's record are the same idea, invented at about the same time.
translations.task: Declare a record TRect with w and h, fill two of them, and print both areas like the C program.
hints: type TRect = record w, h: integer; end;
C's {3, 4} becomes a.w := 3; a.h := 4;

translations.title: var Becomes a Pointer
translations.story: Pascal's var parameters do the pointer work for you. In C, you write it yourself.
translations.task: Write void swap(int *a, int *b) and print the same result as the Pascal program.
hints: var a: integer in Pascal is int *a in C.
Inside, a becomes *a.
The call needs &: swap(&x, &y);

translations.title: repeat … until in BASIC
translations.story: Dartmouth BASIC has no repeat loop. An IF … THEN jump back does the same job.
translations.task: Double 1 until it's above 1000, like the Pascal program, and print the number of doublings and the result on two lines.
hints: repeat … until n > 1000 means: jump back while N <= 1000.
The jump goes to the line that doubles N.

translations.title: Sum on the Panel
translations.story: Dartmouth BASIC adds 1 to 10 in a FOR loop. On the Altair, there is no PRINT, just the lights.
translations.task: Add 1 + 2 + … + 10 with a counting loop (DCR + JNZ) and show the sum on the lights.
translations.source:
10 LET S = 0
20 FOR I = 1 TO 10
30 LET S = S + I
40 NEXT I
50 PRINT S
60 END
hints: Count B down from 10 and add B to A in every round: the order doesn't matter for a sum.
MVI A 0, MVI B 10, loop: ADD B (200), DCR B (005), JNZ loop.
Then OUT 377 and HLT.

translations.title: Stars on the Teletype
translations.story: Both machines from 1975 print to a teletype. The KIM-1 calls OUTCH, the Altair uses OUT 001.
translations.task: Print the same eight stars on the Altair's Teletype with a loop.
translations.source:
OUTCH = $1EA0
LDX #8
LDA #'*
LOOP: JSR OUTCH
DEX
BNE LOOP
BRK
hints: The star '*' is ASCII 42, octal 052.
MVI A 052, MVI B 8, loop: OUT 001, DCR B, JNZ loop, HLT.
LDX/DEX/BNE on the 6502 is MVI B/DCR B/JNZ on the 8080.

translations.title: Count the Bits by Rotating
translations.story: In C, n & 1 and n >>= 1. On the 8080, a rotation drops the lowest bit into the carry.
translations.task: Count the 1 bits of 181 like the C program: rotate A right 8 times, count the carries in C, and show the count on the lights.

requirements.message: Test the carry with JNC or JC.

hints: 181 is octal 265.
loop: RRC, JNC skip, INR C, skip: DCR B, JNZ loop.
MOV A,C (171), OUT 377, HLT.

translations.title: Squares
translations.story: A Dartmouth student's table of squares from 1964. The bank wants it on the mainframe.
translations.task: Print the numbers 1 to 5 and their squares with PERFORM VARYING. Use PIC 9 for the number and PIC Z9 for the square.
translations.source:
10 FOR I = 1 TO 5
20 PRINT I, I*I
30 NEXT I
40 END
translations.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. SQUARES.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.

requirements.message: BASIC's FOR loop is PERFORM VARYING.

hints: FOR I = 1 TO 5 is VARYING I FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL I > 5.
COMPUTE SQ = I * I, MOVE it to an edited field and DISPLAY I " " SQ-OUT.

translations.title: The Till
translations.story: A C program from a shop's cash register, 1985. Accounting wants the same number from COBOL, exact to the cent.
translations.task: Compute the price with VAT in COBOL with COMPUTE … ROUNDED and print it in PIC Z9.99 after TOTAL.
translations.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. TILL.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.
hints: C's double is binary; COBOL's PIC 99V99 is exact decimal.
COMPUTE TOTAL ROUNDED = PRICE * 1.19.

translations.title: The Average
translations.story: A FORTRAN weather job from 1966. The insurance company wants the same average in its COBOL system.
translations.task: Put the five temperatures into a COBOL table (FILLER VALUEs and REDEFINES), add them up in a loop, and print the average with one decimal in PIC ZZ9.9.
translations.source:
DIMENSION T(5)
      DATA T /18.0, 23.0, 31.0, 27.0, 19.0/
      S = 0.0
      DO 10 I = 1, 5
   10 S = S + T(I)
      A = S / 5.0
      WRITE (6, 20) A
   20 FORMAT (9H AVERAGE , F5.1)
      STOP
      END
translations.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. AVERAGE.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.

requirements.message: FORTRAN's DIMENSION is an OCCURS table.
DATA becomes FILLER VALUEs with REDEFINES.
The DO loop is PERFORM VARYING.

hints: 01 TEMP-TABLE REDEFINES TEMP-DATA. 05 TEMP PIC 99 OCCURS 5 TIMES.
COMPUTE AVG ROUNDED = TOTAL / 5 into a PIC 99V9 field, then MOVE it to PIC ZZ9.9.
